message.content: what is the advantage of using matches vs locate that retusn string and bool instead of just a bool ?

content.text:
The advantage is that only one place decides where the root ends.

With `matches` returning a bool, the probe knew the exec path was under a Scoop root but threw away where. Scoop's command then needed the app-dir segment right after that root, so it re-ran the whole search: read the exec path again, read config.json again, resolve symlinks per root again, and repeat the prefix loop, plus a second hand-rolled `Cut` on the default marker. Two detectors had to agree, and the tests covered the copy rather than the probe.

`locate` returning the remainder gives the command the one fact it needs. Scoop's command becomes "first segment of the remainder equals `cli`", with no second search and no duplicate of the marker logic.

The cost is that brew and mise ignore the remainder, so their command funcs carry an unused parameter. If you would rather keep `matches` as a bool, the alternative is a Scoop-specific `scoopAppName(execPath)` that reruns root detection, which is what was there before. I think one extra ignored argument is cheaper than a second detector.

I think that is cheaper than making every reader of the probe wonder what the second return value is for.

Follow-up to #2152.

Users who installed via `install.ps1` currently get the GitHub releases page when Entire reports an update. This prints the README `irm | iex` / `-Channel nightly` commands instead.
